title: Your Brain Believes a Sentence More If It Rhymes

scenes.text: Your brain believes a sentence more if it rhymes.
In two thousand, psychologists showed people old sayings. Half heard the rhyming version. What sobriety conceals, alcohol reveals.
The other half heard the exact same idea without the rhyme. What sobriety conceals, alcohol unmasks.
Same meaning. But people rated the rhyming version as more accurate. More true. And they had no idea the rhyme was doing it.
It happens because rhymes are easier for your brain to process, and your brain mistakes that easy feeling for truth.
Advertisers and lawyers know this. So the next time a slogan sounds right, ask yourself if it just sounds nice. Which rhyme fooled you?

description:
Your brain believes a sentence more if it rhymes.
In a 2000 study published in Psychological Science, people rated rhyming sayings such as What sobriety conceals, alcohol reveals as more accurate than versions with identical meaning that did not rhyme.
Researchers call it the rhyme-as-reason effect: rhymes are easier to process, and the brain mistakes that fluency for truth.
Which rhyming slogan has fooled you?
